## ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- zimmerMANNBuild: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
- zimmerMANNDevImprover: Looks back over completed build work and improves the build chain. Reads the session transcripts and run artefacts for named stories, diagnoses where the loop failed and whose gap it was, checks whether the skills still cite things that are true, and proposes concrete edits to the build skills and loop agents — applied only on Marcel's explicit go.
- zimmerMANNDevOps: Runs deploys, promotions across environments, tags, release cuts and rollbacks on the Zimmermann PWA Kit. Verifies pipeline state live before every action, shows what each environment is running, and executes only on explicit approval. Reports broken gates and stops rather than working around them.
- zimmerMANNPostBuild: The senior dev pass after a build. Audits what zimmerMANNBuild produced against zimmerMANNPreBuild's plan and findings, runs a whole-feature sweep for uniform defects, writes the PR body, and owns the review conversation — pushing and replying only on Marcel's go.
- zimmerMANNPreBuild: The gate and planner before any Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. Gathers and cross-checks every source — Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase and Figma — flags every gap and misalignment, then produces an executable closed-loop build plan and hands off to zimmerMANNBuild. Use at the start of any story, ticket or build task.
- zimmerMANNReview: Reviews someone else's PR as FED Lead. Establishes ground truth, fans out audit angles, verifies every finding before it is raised, then presents for adjudication — Marcel decides the verdict, and comments post only on his go. Loops until the PR is approved.
- zimmerMANNRevImprover: Looks back over completed PR reviews and improves how Marcel reviews. Reads the PR outcome and the review session transcript to judge whether each finding held up, whether anything was missed, and how the review was actually conducted — then proposes concrete edits to zimmerMANNReview, applied only on his explicit go.
- zimmerMANNSprinter: The skill for sprint and agile ceremonies as FED Lead — backlog refinement, sprint planning, standups, retros, and prep for any meeting. Reads Jira and Confluence, drafts what you need to take into the room, and writes to Jira only on your explicit go.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills/session-start

Run the mandatory session start ritual defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do this before writing any code.

## Steps (in order — do not skip any)

1. **Confirm branch** — run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — no edits permitted (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 1). If it matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`, read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) in full before proceeding — the supervised-edit and back-merge rules there apply on top of the Hard Rules.

2. **Read tracking docs** — read these in parallel:
   - [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md) — current phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending
   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**
   - [.docs/memory/feedback.md](../../../.docs/memory/feedback.md) — patterns to avoid or repeat
   - [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) — current `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version and review state
   - [../session-notes.md](../session-notes.md) — lightweight, **gitignored, per-developer** carryover notes from your last local session (a Claude-writable staging area — see "Living Memory" below for how this differs from `.docs/memory/`). If it has pending items, surface them in step 4's "blockers or outstanding issues" and clear/promote each once resolved. It won't exist for a fresh clone or a teammate who hasn't used it — that's expected, skip silently.

3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:
   - `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` — If the script does not exist yet, state that clearly and skip.

4. **State current position** — in plain language, say exactly:
   - Current branch
   - Current sprint / phase (from `projectState.md`)
   - The last completed task and the next task
   - Any blockers or outstanding issues

   Format: "Resuming from: [last completed task]. Next: [next task]. [Any blockers or health issues]."

5. **Confirm readiness** — ask if the user wants to proceed with the stated next task or redirect to something else.

Do not write any code until this ritual is complete and the user has confirmed direction.

---

## Living Memory — what belongs where

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.

**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. It's **not** shared via git — each developer's notes stay local, so they never conflict or overwrite a teammate's. Unlike the files below, Claude may write to it directly. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.

| File | What belongs there | When to update |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture.md` | Stack decisions, overrides pattern, key paths, structural choices | A new integration is added, a structural decision is made, or a key path changes |
| `projectState.md` | Phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending, unresolved dependencies | Any integration goes live, a phase changes, a feature is completed, or a dependency is resolved |
| `feedback.md` | What worked, what failed, patterns to avoid or repeat | After discovering a gotcha, a failed approach, or a validated pattern |
| `references.md` | Service URLs, API keys, credentials, logins, dashboards | A new credential or service URL is introduced (system roles live in `architecture.md`) |
| `userProfile.md` | User's role, expertise, working style, preferences | User shares a preference or working-style detail that should persist |

**Rules:**
- Never leave a file with only its placeholder comment — populate it the moment you learn something that belongs there.
- **No duplication.** Every fact has exactly one home. Before writing something, check whether it already lives in another doc — if it does, reference that doc instead of copying. Applies across all `.md` files: `AGENTS.md`, memory files, and PRDs.
- **Conciseness.** Keep all `.md` instructions concise.

  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.

A SFCC-hosted wishlist for go-live is being scoped but NOT confirmed. ENH-040 still logs an eventual SFCC→Omneo migration. Note: Move-to-Wishlist (CAI-004/008) is **confirmed authenticated-only** at launch — guests are prompted to log in; guest wishlist is a logged enhancement out of scope for go-live.

Intended logic (not yet confirmed): show the Returns link only if the order contains returnable items (via product attribute); window = 15 days from delivery completion date, else 28 days from order creation date if no delivery completion date. Hard dependency: the delivery completion date must be passed back via MuleSoft.
- **Address validation on free-text addresses (CFD-024):** PO Box / Parcel Locker blocking is Confirmed. NEW VR/RT review request (not scoped): "Current magento behaviour lets a user checkout with a very random address with no error messaging. Can this be reviewed?" — broader address-validity enhancement, unscoped.
- **SSO scope (CRM-001):** Sheet only says "to be considered for go-live (ENH tab — to be discussed)". Treat as Open. Note: Social login (Apple/Google) is separately confirmed via ENH-004 (see entry above) and is the only SSO surface in scope for launch.
- **PRC-46 coupon handling at Global-e:** Workbook shows Confirmed 2026-06-24, but sign-off is conditional — "only if Global-e can support." Confirm with Global-e that the SFCC cartridge can apply and validate coupon codes at international checkout before implementing.

PR #70 "feat(pdp): colour swatches and variation selection (SFCC-91)", authored by Jhoan Dela
Cruz (`JhoanDelaCruz`), targets `develop` from
`feature/SFCC-91_pdp-ui-colour-swatches-variation-selection`. Marcel (FED lead) left a
CHANGES_REQUESTED review 2026-08-31 with 3 blocking findings, none yet addressed by Jhoan's two
follow-up commits (836a77b, a9999ec — those only fixed CodeRabbit nits: the
`SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID` fallback and a redundant Storybook `play` block):

1. **Sold-out-everywhere regression**: `suppressColourAttribute` (meant to hide the legacy colour
   picker once the new `ColourSwatches` component takes over) flips back to `false` when every
   colour is unavailable, so the old picker reappears showing every colour as a greyed-out square
   instead of showing nothing. No catalogue product has every colour unavailable, so Marcel
   verified via a standalone script using the real logic rather than live UI — he offered to
   share it.
2. **New Playwright E2E tests don't run**: `e2e/tests/zimm/pdp/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches.spec.js`
   calls 5 fixture functions (`pdpProductWithMultipleColours` + 4 others) that don't exist, and
   expects ~10 `ProductPage` helper methods that were never added. All 11 tests fail against a
   real dev server (not skipped) — the PR description incorrectly claims they skip due to missing
   test data.
3. **Square swatches leaked into the shared `product-view` component**: the circle/square
   selection logic (keyed off the colour attribute) was hardcoded to always-square, unscoped from
   the suppress-flag check — so cart edit modal, wishlist, and bonus-product swatches all became
   square too, breaking the by-design circular swatches in the expanded gallery. Confirmed live in
   the cart edit modal.

On top of Marcel's 3 findings, CI on the latest pushed commit (`a9999ec`, 2026-09-01) has
**Storybook interaction & a11y tests failing**: the `SevenColours` story in
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.stories.tsx` expects 4 rendered
swatch buttons (one pagination page) but gets 7 — pagination isn't slicing the visible set. The
same failure also occurred on an earlier commit on this branch (`195221f`) but a commit in
between (`7513571`) passed — not yet root-caused; flag as a live CI blocker distinct from
Marcel's 3 review comments.

**Why:** this PR cannot merge to `develop` until both the 3 review findings and the CI failure
are resolved — branch protection requires the CHANGES_REQUESTED review to clear and CI to pass.
**How to apply:** before doing any other SFCC-91 work, re-check PR #70's live state
(`gh pr view 70 --json reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup`) — Jhoan may have pushed fixes since
this was recorded. Diff against these 4 known issues rather than re-reviewing from scratch.

follow-up commits (836a77b, a9999ec — those only fixed CodeRabbit nits: the
`SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID` fallback and a redundant Storybook `play` block):

1. **Sold-out-everywhere regression**: `suppressColourAttribute` (meant to hide the legacy colour
   picker once the new `ColourSwatches` component takes over) flips back to `false` when every
   colour is unavailable, so the old picker reappears showing every colour as a greyed-out square
   instead of showing nothing. No catalogue product has every colour unavailable, so Marcel
   verified via a standalone script using the real logic rather than live UI — he offered to
   share it.
2. **New Playwright E2E tests don't run**: `e2e/tests/zimm/pdp/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches.spec.js`
   calls 5 fixture functions (`pdpProductWithMultipleColours` + 4 others) that don't exist, and
   expects ~10 `ProductPage` helper methods that were never added. All 11 tests fail against a
   real dev server (not skipped) — the PR description incorrectly claims they skip due to missing
   test data.
3. **Square swatches leaked into the shared `product-view` component**: the circle/square
   selection logic (keyed off the colour attribute) was hardcoded to always-square, unscoped from
   the suppress-flag check — so cart edit modal, wishlist, and bonus-product swatches all became
   square too, breaking the by-design circular swatches in the expanded gallery. Confirmed live in
   the cart edit modal.

On top of Marcel's 3 findings, CI on the latest pushed commit (`a9999ec`, 2026-09-01) has
**Storybook interaction & a11y tests failing**: the `SevenColours` story in
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.stories.tsx` expects 4 rendered
swatch buttons (one pagination page) but gets 7 — pagination isn't slicing the visible set. The
same failure also occurred on an earlier commit on this branch (`195221f`) but a commit in
between (`7513571`) passed — not yet root-caused; flag as a live CI blocker distinct from
Marcel's 3 review comments.

**Why:** this PR cannot merge to `develop` until both the 3 review findings and the CI failure
are resolved — branch protection requires the CHANGES_REQUESTED review to clear and CI to pass.
**How to apply:** before doing any other SFCC-91 work, re-check PR #70's live state
(`gh pr view 70 --json reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup`) — Jhoan may have pushed fixes since
this was recorded. Diff against these 4 known issues rather than re-reviewing from scratch.

## Phase 1 — ground truth. Yours, not an agent's.

### Frame the PR

Base SHA, head SHA, files changed, ±lines. **Use the live head** — a stale ref has already caused a
whole round of re-verification here.

### Requirements — Jira, Confluence, Figma

Build the same requirements picture a PreBuild would build, then judge the PR against it. Every
scope argument, every "this is missing", every "this wasn't asked for" gets decided against these
words — not the PR description's paraphrase of them.

**Jira.** Pull the full ticket: description, ACs, linked work items, and — critically — the full
comment thread. Decisions made in comments routinely contradict the description and never make it
back into the ACs. Flag: untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments
· a linked blocker still open · a decision in comments that the implementation may not have seen ·
**evidence that a different PR, branch, or assignee is already working the same ticket.**

**Anything flagged here goes in your next status update to Marcel, even when it's correctly out
of scope for the PR itself.** "Not my concern for this review" and "not worth telling him" are
different judgements — a discovery can be exactly right to leave alone in the diff and still be
something he needs to know exists. Deciding not to act on it is not the same as deciding not to
mention it.

**Confluence.** If the ticket links a PRD, TSD, or integration doc, read it. The Jira ACs are
often a summary; the full requirements live in Confluence. Flag: a Confluence requirement not
reflected in the ACs · a doc that contradicts the ticket · a doc that describes an approach the
PR does not follow.

**Figma.** Read the design systematically — not just the node cited in the PR description.

- **All variants and states:** hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty, selected.
  A state the PR doesn't implement is a finding; a state Figma doesn't specify is an open
  question to name, not a reason to skip. **Before concluding a state is simply absent from a
  component, check whether an adjacent or parent element carries that same signal instead** (the
  button not the swatch, the row not the cell) — a concern can be fully handled by the design and
  still look like a gap if you only look at the one element it doesn't live on.
- **Annotations:** interaction notes and spacing/token callouts often hold the real spec detail.
- **Currency:** is the linked node archived or superseded? An archived node that still renders
  is a trap — triage before judging.
- **Tokenisation:** does every colour, spacing, and type value map to an existing `--zimm-*`
  token, or did the author introduce a new one? A new token is Tier 1; confirm it was handled
  correctly.
- **Measurement:** FRAMES and INSTANCES report real boxes (comparable to CSS). TEXT nodes report
  cap-height (not comparable). Never file a mismatch from a TEXT node. Never cross-compare the
  Design System file and the Designs file — they are different sources.

**If the Jira-linked nodes are incomplete, partial, or outdated — stop and ask Marcel for the
correct nodes before continuing.** One node URL per variant and per state, not one per component.
Do not guess at a neighbouring node that looks close, do not proceed on a partial picture, and do
not treat an archived node as the spec. The whole review hangs on having the right design source;
a wrong node produces false findings and misses real ones. This is the one step where asking
beats estimating.

The visual checklist in Phase 2 tells you what to verify in the browser. This step tells you
**what to look for** — you cannot run that checklist without knowing what the design intended.

### The rubric

`.claude/rules/*`, `AGENTS.md`, and the exemplar PR the work should follow. These are what the PR
is judged against — a reviewer applying general best practice instead of house rules generates
noise that reads like signal.

**If the PR edits the rule files it would be judged against, read the rubric at the BASE commit.**
Judging a PR against its own edited rules is circular. Rule-file edits are reviewed separately, as
changes.

### Run the gates yourself — on head and on base

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test
npm run lint
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Then run them again at the base SHA. **Without a baseline you cannot tell a failure the PR
introduced from one it inherited**, and inherited debt reported as a new violation is the fastest
way to lose a reviewer's trust.

Three false signals, all seen on this repo:

1. **Non-zero at a healthy baseline.** `lint` and `audit:tokens` both exit non-zero on a clean
   tree. Compare counts; ignore exit codes.
2. **A pass having run nothing.** `vitest.config.ts` sets `passWithNoTests: true` — a typo'd path
   filter exits 0 having run zero tests. **Assert on the reported item count, never the exit code.**
3. **A skipped required check looks green.** `detect-changes` can skip `unit-tests` and
   `storybook-test` entirely, and the PR still shows mergeable. Report which checks actually
   *executed* versus which were skipped. A skip proves nothing.

### CodeRabbit is an input, not a verdict

If CodeRabbit has reviewed, read it — then verify it. It has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this
repo. Its findings enter Phase 2 as claims to test, exactly like anyone else's.

## Phase 2 — audit

### Fan out

`zm-tester` dispatches reviewers on **distinct but overlapping** briefs. The overlap is the
mechanism: two agents converging independently is your confidence signal; two disagreeing is where
you learn something.

Give each: the diff, the ticket verbatim, and **your measured gate numbers — then forbid them from
re-running the gates.** Their budget goes on what the gates cannot see.

Angles that have earned their place: correctness and regression · conventions, structure and tier
ownership · contract fidelity, if the PR ports, wraps or overrides something · failure modes and
security · token and styling strategy (bandaid tokens, missing semantic tokens, state
exhaustiveness).

**Design fidelity is yours, not an agent's.** Agents have no browser and no Figma access — ask
them to reason from code and they will, but they cannot see what renders. For any PR that changes
rendered output, run this checklist yourself at the PR's head:

| What to check | How |
|---|---|
| Dimensions and spacing match Figma frames | DevTools computed, vs. Figma inspect |
| Colours resolve to the correct semantic token | DevTools → Computed → colour value |
| Typography uses `textStyle=`, not raw `fontSize` | DevTools → font-size is a `var()` |
| All designed states render correctly (hover, focus, active, disabled) | Tab through + `:hov` in DevTools |
| Responsive behaviour matches the spec | Resize or toggle responsive mode |
| No visual regressions on adjacent components | Scroll the surrounding page |

If a state is not in the PR's recipe at all, no agent will flag it — only you will notice. The
visual checkpoint is the only gate on design fidelity.

Use **fresh contexts, not forks.** A fork inherits your assumptions about what "done" looks like,
which is exactly what you want tested.

### Scope

`zm-orchestrator` returns the scope verdict — does this PR deliver its ticket, neither under nor
over. Both directions carry equal weight.

### Verify the findings before they reach you

`zm-scorer`, briefed in **findings mode** — it is not scoring the PR, it is scoring the claims:

> For each finding: does it survive scrutiny? Reproduce it or say you could not. Return
> **CONFIRMED** (reproduced from source), **PLAUSIBLE** (consistent with what you read, decisive
> evidence missing — say exactly what would settle it), or **UNSUPPORTED** (the citation does not
> support the claim; say what is actually true). Where a finding's conclusion is broader than its
> search supports, downgrade it — that is the single most common failure mode. Any "X exists
> nowhere" claim must state its search scope in the same sentence.

Expect roughly a third to be wrong. You should not be adjudicating unverified claims.

**This applies to your own findings too, not just an agent's.** Anything you notice directly
while gathering ground truth (a comparison against a related PR, a claim sitting in a code
comment, an assumption about what a value implies) gets the same CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED
discipline before it is presented as fact — a finding is not exempt from scrutiny just because no
agent produced it. Route it through the same questions: what is the search scope, does one
uncorroborated source actually settle this, and has a stated number been measured or only assumed.

### Classify every survivor

- **In-scope defect** — belongs to this PR. Only these can become comments.
- **Out-of-scope** — real, but not this PR's problem. Name the owning ticket or the person.
- **Nitpick** — cosmetic, brings no value. Recorded, never posted.

A true finding raised on the wrong PR is still noise.

---

## Phase 3 — adjudicate

### Present, in "ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead" register

1. **Gate table** — head versus base, with which checks actually executed
2. **Findings, ranked by what it costs to ignore** — not by severity label, by consequence.
   Each with `file:line`, CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, and its classification
3. **The scope verdict**
4. **What nobody verified** — the honest section, and what stops a clean result reading as proof
5. **Your adjudications to make**, one at a time via AskUserQuestion

### The verdict is yours

**Approve or request changes is your call, and so is every disputed finding.** The agents produce
findings; you decide what they mean. Where two reviewers disagree, go to source yourself — do not
average them, and do not take the more confident one. Confidence and correctness are not correlated
in agent output.

Name one premise every reviewer agreed on, and make someone attack it.

### Then the comments

Draft general and inline comments for the in-scope defects only. Structure that has worked:

- Verdict up front
- The small cleanups separated from the one thing that genuinely needs the author's call
- A blocker framed as **a question about intent**, citing the project's own doc by section
- The two acceptable resolutions named
- Where an independent tool corroborated, say so

**Natural human language without sacrificing the technical accuracy.** No em-dashes. No Claude or
CodeRabbit attribution. No citation of any local-only doc — cite `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`
instead, which the author can actually open. No opening praise or thanks before the substance — a
review comment states findings, it does not warm up first. Watch for jargon-stacking too: a
sentence naming three technical concepts back to back reads like documentation, not like one
person explaining something to another — split it or say it plainer instead.

**Never reveal that a parallel or competing implementation of the same ticket exists**, even in
passing ("the other version of this feature," "the other build") — a review comment is visible to
the whole team, and disclosing a second, independent attempt at the same story is not this
reviewer's call to make. When a content rule like this applies, sweep every drafted comment for
it before presenting the batch, not just the one currently under discussion — a rule caught on
one comment and missed on a near-identical one is a leak, not a style nit.

**Nothing posts until you say so.** Show the full set, post the batch on your go.

---

## The loop

The author pushes changes. Re-review.

**Scoped by default:** which findings the new commits resolved, which they missed, and whether the
fixes introduced anything new. Settled items are not re-litigated.

**Full pass when the diff has genuinely moved** — a substantial new commit, or a change to the
approach rather than the details. **Say which one you ran.**

Repeat until approved. Confirm your own requested changes actually landed rather than taking
"done" on trust.

---

## Ownership and phrasing — every outward-facing surface

Every finding names **who resolves it**: the author, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question — never a directive.** "Should this
route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before posting, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as hiding
behind their authority.

**Be scrupulously fair to the author.** Separate "broke a documented rule" from "hit a gap the
process never covered", and where the process failed them, say so. Flag explicitly any finding
where the fact is true but the characterisation is unfair — better to drop a finding than post an
unfair one.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** This skill reviews. If a fix is needed on your own branch, that is Build.
- **Never post a comment, a review, or a verdict without an explicit go.**
- **Never resolve a thread you did not open.**
- **Never report inherited debt as a new violation.** Baseline first.
- **Never flag out-of-scope findings onto the PR.** Record them for yourself.
- **Say what you could not verify.** A review that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016GTGo4ZCJGFzLwjsqmwitY","messageHeadline":"fix(header): set logo to fixed per-breakpoint dimensions","oid":"61f756ed3bfd321a5828e81930bdd2e9b245fdf8"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-26T23:49:23Z","authors":[{"email":"tim+1@lavelle.bio","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjY0NDU3MTA=","login":"TimLavelle","name":"TimLavelle"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Sonnet 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-26T23:49:23Z","messageBody":"Three compounding bugs, found and fixed in sequence while matching
the logo to Figma's 223x26 mobile / 758x115 tablet+desktop spec:

1. ZimmLogo took a plain DOM `style` prop, which can only ever hold
   one unconditional value — passing a Chakra responsive array through
   it just stringified to garbage ("223px,,758px,12"). ZimmLogo now
   renders via chakra.svg and accepts an `sx` prop (Chakra's own
   style-prop system, which actually resolves responsive values into
   real media queries) alongside the existing `style` for simple
   static overrides.
2. Even through `sx`, sizing still lost to base SFCC's own `logo` part
   (width: [8,8,8,12] Chakra-spacing array) at md/lg — Chakra's
   multi-part recipe merge combines our Header.css.ts override with
   that base part in a way that isn't a reliable per-key override for
   this specific key, regardless of array vs. fully-named-object
   responsive syntax. Logo sizing now bypasses that merge entirely:
   removed from header.css.ts's `logo` part, set instead as a plain
   HEADER_LOGO_SX object passed directly to <ZimmLogo sx={...}> in
   header/index.tsx — a plain object spread, no base theme involved.
3. ZimmLogo's own base sx sets maxWidth: 327px as a generic default,
   which survived the merge with HEADER_LOGO_SX (that object only set
   width/height) and silently capped the 758px desktop/tablet target.
   HEADER_LOGO_SX now explicitly sets maxWidth: 'none'.

=== SUMMARY/STATUS ===
SFCC-52 - Global Header UI
status: Code Review | assignee: Tim Lavelle | reporter: Jasmijn Tsang

=== DESCRIPTION ===
**As a** Shopper, 
**I want** to see a consistent global header on every page, 
**so that** I can always access key navigation and account features regardless of where I am on the site.

Reference image (Figma is leading):

!["image-20260618-040938.png"](image-20260618-040938.png)

----

The global header is a sticky component displayed at the top of every page across all storefronts and devices. It contains the Zimmermann logo, header icons. The header remains visible as the shopper scrolls down the page.

This story covers the **header shell and layout only** — the visual structure, component placement, and sticky behaviour. Icon destinations (Search, Account, Wish List, Cart) are wired up as the underlying pages and features are built in their respective stories. The exception is the logo (links to homepage).

**Header elements:**

  - **Zimmermann logo/wordmark* — left aligned with and below the top categories in the header, links back to the homepage on click
  - **Navigation menu -* based on the latest Figma design, left-aligned top-level categories include: NEW, CLOTHING, ACCESSORIES, COLLECTIONS, Z.IMMERSE. For this user story, we will set up the first basis of the navigation items in SFCC.
  - **Header icons (right-aligned):* Search, Account, Bag, Wishlist, Bag; displayed as visual elements - destination page in other stories.

**Responsive behaviour:** There is a header design for both desktop and mobile.

=== COMMENTS ===
--- Tim Lavelle 2026-07-26T08:08:00.911+1000 ---
Hey User:5cc71886cbbec211ec62929d , I had review of this card and a little bit like the story we reviewed last week, here are my thoughts on a few changes to the Acceptance Criteria section:

  - **Desktop & Mobile*
      - I think 5 & 6 belong with the Cart user story
        - With the Cart, is there any designs on what happens if they click on the cart? If so, that Design would also be part of the Cart user story. 
  - **Mobile*
      - I think 8 - 11 should be placed in the Navigation user story as that’s behaviour we need to build into the nav CSS & JS

Hopefully not too much work to move around, but happy to have a call and discuss as well. 

Thanks Jas!

TO: *Content Type*

# Given the Contentful content type is created, when a Site Merchandiser opens the content model, then it includes nav item label, category ID, display order, and storefront scoping.
# Given a Site Merchandiser updates and publishes the nav entries in Contentful, when the page loads after publishing, then the updated nav items and ordering are reflected across all storefronts without a code deployment.

*Structure — Desktop*

# Given a shopper visits any page on desktop, when the page loads, then the Navigation component renders with top-level nav items displayed left-aligned in the configured order.
# Given a shopper visits any page on desktop, when the page loads, then Search Bar, Account, Wishlist and Bag icons are displayed right-aligned in the nav bar.
# Given a shopper opens a mega menu on desktop, when the mega menu is active, then the four icons are replaced by a CLOSE X control on the right side of the nav
# Given a shopper clicks CLOSE X on desktop, when the control is activated, then the mega menu is dismissed and the four icons are restored.

*Structure — Tablet*

# Given a shopper visits any page on tablet, when the page loads, then the Navigation component renders with all top-level nav items and all four icons visible (Search, Account, Wishlist, Bag)
# Given a shopper opens a mega menu on tablet, when the mega menu is active, then the four icons are replaced by CLOSE X on the right side of the nav.
# Given a shopper clicks CLOSE X on tablet, when the control is activated, then the mega menu is dismissed and the four icons are restored.

*Structure — Mobile*

# Given a shopper visits any page on mobile, when the page loads, then the Navigation component renders with a hamburger icon on the left and Search and Bag icons on the right. Top-level nav items are not visible.
# Given a shopper opens the mobile drawer, when the drawer is active, then the hamburger icon is replaced by a close icon on the left. Search and Bag icons remain visible on the right.
# Given a shopper taps the close icon on mobile, when activated, then the mobile drawer is dismissed and the hamburger icon is restored.

*Category Taxonomy*

# Given the Navigation component renders, when it reads top-level nav items, then items, their display order, and storefront visibility are managed in Contentful using a category ID to reference the SFCC category taxonomy in BM (SFCC-28) and are not hardcoded in the component.
# Given a nav item corresponds to an SFCC category, when a shopper clicks it, then they are navigated to the corresponding category PLP.
# Given the Navigation component fetches top-level nav items from Contentful, when it renders, then it uses the storefront-specific configuration ensuring nav items and their ordering reflect the correct regional setup.
# Given a nav item is unpublished or not configured in Contentful for a specific storefront, when the Navigation component renders on that storefront, then the corresponding nav item does not appear in the headline nav.

*Search*

# Given a shopper clicks the search icon in the header, when the interaction occurs, then they are navigated to the search experience - [https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-113|https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-113|smart-link] 

*Wishlist*

# Given a shopper views the header and their wishlist is empty, when the component renders, then the wishlist icon displays in its outlined state.
# Given a shopper views the header and their wishlist contains one or more items, when the component renders, then the wishlist icon displays in its filled state.

*Cart*

# Given a shopper views the header, when the cart contains items, then the cart icon displays a dynamic item count — full cart behaviour is covered in the dynamic cart header story - [https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-827|https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-827|smart-link] 

*Accessibility*

# Given a screen reader user is navigating by landmarks, when they reach the main navigation, then it is wrapped in a nav element with aria-label equal to Main navigation, distinguishing it from any other nav regions on the page.
# Given a screen reader user navigates the headline nav, when they move through the top-level items, then each item is announced correctly and the number of items is communicated via a list structure.
# Given a keyboard-only user is navigating the header on desktop or tablet, when they Tab through the headline nav, then each top-level item and icon receives focus in left-to-right order.
# Given a screen reader user navigates to a top-level item that triggers a mega menu, when the item receives focus and the menu is closed, then the item is announced with aria-haspopup true and aria-expanded false.
# Given a screen reader user activates a mega menu trigger, when the menu opens, then aria-expanded updates to true and the CLOSE X control is focusable and announced as Close menu.
# Given a screen reader user navigates to Z.IMMERSE, when the item receives focus, then it is announced as a standard link with no aria-haspopup or aria-expanded attributes.
# Given a keyboard-only user is on mobile with the drawer closed, when they Tab to the hamburger button, then it is announced as Open navigation menu with aria-expanded false.
# Given a keyboard-only user opens the mobile drawer, when the drawer is active, then the close icon is announced as Close navigation menu with aria-expanded true.
# Given a keyboard-only user is interacting with the nav on any device, when they interact with any element, then all interactions are achievable without a mouse.

content.text: Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/figma/2.2.96/skills/figma-design-to-code # Implement a Figma Design as Code (Design → Code) Use this skill to turn a Figma design into code in a target codebase. This is the **read-FROM-Figma** direction: pull design context out of Figma with `get_design_context`, then adapt it into the project's real stack. For the reverse direction — building or updating a design *in* Figma from code — use [figma-generate-design](../figma-generate-design/SKILL.md) instead. This skill owns the **workflow** for design-to-code. Parameter mechanics (nodeId / fileKey / branchKey extraction, URL parsing, `format`/`query` options, response shape) live on the `get_design_context` tool description itself — follow them there. **Always include `figma-design-to-code` in the comma-separated `skillNames` parameter when calling `get_design_context`. If this skill was loaded via an MCP resource, you MUST prefix the name with `resource:` (e.g. `resource:figma-design-to-code`).** This is a logging parameter used to track skill usage — it does not affect execution. ## Direction and Scope - You MUST use this skill for design → code: implementing, translating, or porting a Figma node into code. - You MUST NOT use this skill to write to Figma. ## Workflow ### 1. Call get_design_context first - You MUST call `get_design_context` on the target node before writing any code. It is your primary tool — a single call returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual hints. - You MUST NOT reach for `get_metadata` or `get_screenshot` as a substitute. Use them only to orient (e.g. picking a node) or to validate, not in place of `get_design_context`. ### 2. Treat the output as a reference, not final code - The returned code is React + Tailwind enriched with hints. You MUST treat it as a REFERENCE, not as final code to paste verbatim. - You MUST adapt it to the target project's language, framework, component library, styling system, and conventions. Match the surrounding code. ### 3. Reuse what the project already has - Before writing new code, You MUST check the target project for existing components, layout patterns, and design tokens that match the design intent. - You MUST reuse the project's existing components and tokens instead of generating new equivalents from scratch. ### 4. Honor the response hints by priority Apply the hints in this order — earlier sources override later ones: 1. **Code Connect snippets** → use the mapped codebase component directly. 2. **Component documentation links** → follow them for usage and guidelines. 3. **Design annotations** → follow any designer notes or constraints. 4. **Design tokens (CSS variables)** → map them to the project's token system. 5. **Raw hex / absolute positioning** → loosely structured; lean on the screenshot for intent. ### 5. Reproduce images and icons faithfully Images and icons come back as `` elements whose `src` is a remote asset URL (`https://.../api/mcp/asset/...`). Apply these rules as you write the code: - **Render every icon/image from its exported asset.** Never hand-write or inline `` to fill it (`100%` or fixed px) — never `auto`, which blows the image up to its intrinsic size. ## Error Recovery - On a `get_design_context` error, STOP and read the message before retrying. - If the design URL has no `node-id` (a file-only URL), ask the user for a node-specific URL — You MUST NOT guess or pass an empty `nodeId`. - On a timeout, retry against a smaller node or selection. - You MUST NOT silently fall back to hand-writing the screen from the screenshot alone when `get_design_context` can still provide context.

12:## 1. Global Header (HPC-015 – HPC-028)
14:- **Sticky** on scroll, all pages and devices (HPC-015, confirmed). Mobile unsticky-on-scroll behaviour (header reappears on scroll-up, à la Jacquemus) is a **new design requirement pending design prototype** — do not implement until the prototype is delivered.
15:- Brand logo links to homepage (HPC-016, confirmed). **Three logo behaviour scenarios flagged** — to be defined per designs before implementation.
16:- **Rotating promotional announcement banner** above the header — CMS-managed via Contentful (HPC-017, confirmed).
18:### Header icons (HPC-018 — Confirmed)
19:The confirmed header icon set is: **Search, Account, and Bag** (HPC-018). Locate Boutique, Contact Us, and Newsletter are **not part of the header** — confirmed per design review on 23 June 2026. Placement of those three icons elsewhere (footer or other location) remains design-dependent and will follow the new UX designs.
21:- **Wishlist icon**: anonymous → redirects to login (HPC-019, confirmed — guest wishlist explicitly **not in scope for launch** per 25/05 review; logged to enhancement log); logged-in → wishlist page (HPC-020, confirmed)
22:- **Bag icon**: displays running item count (HPC-021, confirmed)
23:- **Country/region selector**: visible in header on all storefronts **except AU** (HPC-026, confirmed — AU is the default/x-default storefront and has no selector). The selector also appears in the **footer**, in addition to the header (HPC-026, confirmed). On mobile it is additionally surfaced within the **hamburger/burger menu** (HPC-025, confirmed). No international pages exist yet (HPC-026 design note). See [regional.md](regional.md) for selector behaviour.
24:- Region selection persists across sessions (HPC-027, confirmed)
25:- Business users can add/remove navigation items without a code change (HPC-028, confirmed)
28:- **Mobile unstick-on-scroll** (HPC-015) — new design requirement (Jacquemus-style reappear-on-scroll-up); pending design prototype. Base sticky behaviour confirmed; designs currently do not show the header as sticky.
29:- **Logo behaviour** (HPC-016) — 3 logo behaviour scenarios flagged, to be defined per designs.
33:## 2. Navigation (HPC-022 – HPC-025, HPC-029)
35:- Top-level categories link to PLP (HPC-022, confirmed — design dependency: each top-level item is either a mega menu trigger or a direct page link)
36:- **"Back in Boutique"** is a manually curated navigation category routing to its own PLP (HPC-023, confirmed)
37:- **Desktop**: mega menu on hover — with the exception of **Z.Immerse**, which functions as a direct link to a page, not a mega menu trigger (HPC-024, confirmed)
38:- **Mobile**: hamburger menu (HPC-025, confirmed). The country/region selector is also surfaced within the mobile hamburger/burger menu (HPC-025, confirmed — placement detail). Selector scope is all storefronts except AU (HPC-026).
39:- The system supports **cloning of the global navigation structure across markets** (HPC-029, confirmed)
43:## 3. Homepage Content (HPC-001 – HPC-012)
45:- Contentful is the sole CMS across all regional storefronts (HPC-001, confirmed). Integration is via the Salesforce App Exchange connector, consuming content through the Contentful delivery API for all customer-facing pages (Third Party Integrations — CMS / Contentful). Homepage carries product names only, which sit in Contentful.
46:- All images and video assets managed through the **Contentful media library** (HPC-003, confirmed)
47:- Video referenced via **embed URL** within CMS content entries (HPC-004, confirmed). Vimeo video is supported on editorial pages via URL embed, with the embed URL stored in the CMS (Third Party Integrations — Media / Vimeo)
48:- Locale-specific homepage content across all regional storefronts (HPC-005, confirmed)
49:- Regional authors can publish locale-specific content without affecting other storefronts (HPC-007, confirmed)
50:- **Full-width hero banner** with CMS-managed imagery, copy and CTA links; supports full bleed or padded, square or portrait (HPC-008, confirmed)
51:- **Editorial modules**: campaign imagery, collection features, product spotlights (HPC-009, confirmed)
52:- Global/local content model: some content global (e.g. Sustainability, Fashion Show Hub), some localised (e.g. policy pages). Homepage is rarely global (HPC-011, confirmed)
58:- **Contentful vs SFCC scope split** (HPC-001, HPC-002, HPC-006, HPC-010, HPC-012) — pending discussion with Contentful. Affects whether product names/prices sit in Contentful or SFCC ("EK - If we are displaying Product names and Potentially prices this would sit on SFCC").
59:- **Contentful preview environment** (HPC-002) — no primary sign-off; challenged: "EK - As we have a Contentful Studio license - is this required?" Studio licence may make a separate preview environment redundant.
60:- **Media library download allowance** (HPC-003) — open action on Zimmermann to confirm 12,000 GB/month is sufficient for peak trade; licence may need revising.
61:- **Transperfect translation workflow** (HPC-006) — no primary sign-off; challenged: "EK - We need to discuss the translation strategy/workflow." Preference: translation memory/workflow in the CMS with a Transperfect integration for human review. Full workflow to be agreed.
62:- **Reusable page builder templates** (HPC-010) — no primary sign-off; challenged: "is this required? DR: The ability to reuse an existing template is needed... Is this possible within Studio?" Feasibility within Contentful Studio pending.
63:- **Live stream embedding via structured CMS solution** (HPC-012) — no primary sign-off; pending Contentful vs SFCC scope split.
67:## 4. Didomi Consent Notice (HPC-013 – HPC-014, confirmed)
69:- Didomi consent notice **greys out all site content** and prevents interaction with all site elements while displayed (HPC-013, confirmed — subject to designs)
70:- Grey-out is removed and full site interactivity restored once the customer has completed the consent flow (HPC-014, confirmed)
76:## 5. Global Footer (HPC-030 – HPC-033, HPC-038, confirmed)
78:- Global footer with content managed via Contentful, editable per website or locale (HPC-030, confirmed)
79:- Footer navigation links (HPC-031, confirmed) navigate to the relevant page or destination on click (HPC-032, confirmed)
80:- Copyright and legal text in the footer (HPC-033, confirmed)
81:- Business users can add region-specific footer links — e.g. Acknowledgement of Country on AU storefront (HPC-038, confirmed)
82:- **Country/region selector** also appears in the footer (in addition to the header), on all storefronts except AU (HPC-026, confirmed). See section 1 and [regional.md](regional.md).
86:## 6. "Join Us" Email Capture (HPC-034 – HPC-037, confirmed)
88:- "Join Us" email capture field in the footer (HPC-034, confirmed)
89:- On clicking the Continue CTA, a **modal** collects the customer's **first name and last name** (HPC-035, confirmed)
90:- Sign-up data passed to **Omneo**, which then forwards to **Emarsys** (HPC-036, confirmed)
91:- Sign-up modal displays appropriate privacy consent copy, a link to the local Privacy Policy, **and an accessibility disclaimer** (HPC-037, confirmed)
96:## 7. Inside Chat (HPC-039 – HPC-040, confirmed)
98:- Chat widget displayed as a pop-up overlay on relevant pages; page visibility rules determined by Inside Chat (HPC-039, confirmed)
100:- Chat widget must only be initialised **after Didomi consent** for the relevant cookie category (HPC-040, confirmed)

{"body":"# Description

Removes `BP.tabletWide` (53.75em / 860px) and its single call site. It was our own
invention, not a design constraint, and it was making the tablet footer worse.

The footer misbehaves across the tablet band in three ways — the email field crowding the
nav groups, nav labels wrapping, and the bottom bar growing 14px taller. All three share a
root cause: fixed-width pieces in a shrinking box with `flexWrap: nowrap` closing the only
escape route. **This PR fixes one specific contributor to that, not the root cause.**

`tabletWide` stepped `linksInner`'s gap from `3xl` (40px) to `5xl` (80px) at 860px. The nav
columns reach their natural width (115/135/106) around 836px and stop wrapping — and then at
860px this rule spent 40px more on gaps than the row had, squeezing them back below content
width and re-wrapping labels that had just recovered.

Kiera confirmed the Figma Footer component has exactly three size variants, read off the
comps' own min/max widths: **Mobile 320–767, Tablet 768–1023, Desktop 1024+**. There is no
fourth variant. Our other two breakpoints (`tablet` 768, `desktop` 1024) match hers exactly;
this one had nothing behind it.

Measured across 768–1024 in 2px steps against a built Storybook:

| | broken ranges | span |
|---|---|---|
| before | 768–832 **and 860–912** | ~124px |
| after | 768–834 | **~68px** |

> **What this does not fix, and why it isn't in scope.** 768–834 still breaks. The email
> column is a fixed 320px that never shrinks, so at 768px the nav block gets 368px to fit
> 436px of content — 68px short. Closing it means something has to flex, and which one is a
> design decision: narrow the email field to 240px, let the nav wrap to two rows, or tighten
> the gaps. All three are measured and drafted for the UI designer; none belongs in a PR that
> removes an unbacked breakpoint.

# Linked

- Follows up: **SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI), merged in #59 — this is a defect in what that
  shipped. No ticket exists for footer responsive work; `gh issue list` and a sweep of
  `.docs/`/`.claude/` turned up nothing, so this is deliberately unticketed rather than
  mislinked.
- Sprint: SFCC — Sprint 5

> With no `SFCC-\d+` key in the title, body or branch name, `e2e-browserstack` will not run
> at all. That is `qa.yml`'s designed behaviour, not a failure — with nothing to attribute
> results to in Zephyr, there is nothing correct to run.

# Squad ownership

- [x] Cross-squad — both leads notified

`components/footer/` is Tier 2 Global Shell owned by both squads. `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
lists footer under Squad A but instructs notifying Squad B before any change; #59 shipped it
as Squad B.

# Types of Changes

- [x] **Bug fix** (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

# Changes

- `components/footer/footer.css.ts` — removed the `@media (min-width: ${BP.tabletWide})`
  block on `linksInner` (three lines; a `gap` step from `3xl` to `5xl`)
- `theme/components/footerShared.ts` — removed the `tabletWide` entry from `BP`, and recorded
  why at the point of use so it is not reintroduced. `tablet` and `desktop` are unchanged
- `.claude/registry/{components,hooks}.md` — **mechanical, and none of it is mine.** The
  `pre-commit` hook regenerates and stages the registry on any `components/` edit. The
  consumer-count changes (`Icons` 10→7, `Link` 25→24, `Register` 14→13) are **develop's own
  staleness**: its registry was last generated 2026-08-26T17:51, before #62 removed dead
  components. Verified by checking out `develop` and running `generateRegistry.mjs` — it
  produces those exact values with no change of mine present. Skip those hunks.

# How to test-drive this PR

- The branch gets its own MRT preview URL automatically — open the footer and drag the window
  from 768 to 1024. Nothing should re-wrap once it settles at ~836px
- `npm run build-storybook`, serve it, open `Layout/Footer → Default` and step the viewport
  through 856 → 864. Before: columns collapse to 97/114/89 at 860 and labels wrap. After:
  they hold 115/135/106
- "Acknowledgement of Country" wraps at every width including 1440 — that is by design;
  Figma's own item is two lines and the 160px column cap reproduces it

# Protection-tier check

> **No Tier 1 file is modified by this PR.**
>
> ⚠️ **Tier 2** — `overrides/app/theme/components/footerShared.ts` (**UI-Designer-owned**).
> `protectedFiles.md:41-43` names this file explicitly as staying Tier 2 because it holds
> genuinely cross-component shared values that co-location does not cover. The change is one
> deleted constant plus a comment; no design value moves.
>
> `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` sits inside a Tier 2 directory but is
> **not** governed by that tier's designer gate — CODEOWNERS `:186`
> (`overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts`) is the last matching rule and routes it to the
> owning squads only, per `protectedFiles.md:39-41`.

This change therefore spans two ownership surfaces (Tier 2 designer-owned, Tier 3
squad-owned). Flagged per AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 rather than split, since removing the
constant without its call site — or vice versa — would leave the repo in a worse state than
either end point.

# Testing

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean. Not wired into CI; this is the only place it runs
- [x] `npm run lint` — 19 problems (4 errors / 15 warnings), **identical to `develop`**.
      Neither changed source file appears in the output. The 4 errors are pre-existing
      `prettier/prettier` in `routes.tsx` and `recipeGuards.test.ts`
- [x] `npm run test` (Vitest) — 379 passed / 25 files
- [x] Storybook interaction + a11y — 98 passed / 23 suites. `preview.tsx` sets
      `a11y: {test: 'error'}`, so every story is also an axe assertion
- [x] `npm run audit:tokens` — 4 unacknowledged, **identical to `develop`**. Re-checked after
      the comment edit: `footerShared.ts`'s `audit-allow` marker still associates and both its
      values remain acknowledged
- [x] Local CodeRabbit (`cr review --light --base develop`) — **no findings**
- [x] `/code-quality` vs `develop` — 0 must-fix, 0 should-fix. Two backlog notes below
- [x] **Browser measurement** — `Layout/Footer → Default` swept 768–1024 in 2px steps against
      a built Storybook. Broken span ~124px → ~68px; 856–864 holds 115/135/106 with no
      wrapping. Futura Round confirmed loaded (151.8px vs 167.3px fallback for "BOOK AN
      APPOINTMENT"), so these are real-font break points
- **Not verified by any automated test: the fix itself.** No Storybook viewport addon is
      registered and `preview.tsx` sets no viewport, so the runner uses Playwright's default
      1280×720 — above `BP.desktop`. **The removed rule was never active in any Storybook
      run.** The 98 passing tests prove no regression; they are not evidence the fix works.
      That evidence is the developer-run measurement above and is not reproducible in CI
- **N/A: Playwright.** `e2e/tests/` holds one homepage smoke spec. A footer spec is gated on
      Lead QA signing off a Gherkin `.feature` first, per the three-stage workflow

# Known gaps and follow-ups

- **768–834 still breaks** — needs a design decision on which element flexes. Three options
  measured: email field to 240px (keeps one row and restores 44px separation, footer height
  unchanged); nav wraps to two rows (keeps the 320px field, footer grows ~175px); or tighten
  everything (fits, but the field and nav still touch)
- **Bottom bar** — "Terms & Conditions" wraps to two lines below ~909px, making that bar 93px
  instead of 79px. Same root cause, separate fix
- **`BP.desktop` (1024) vs `gridSystem.xl` (1280)** — the footer switches to its desktop
  layout 256px before the page grid does. May be intentional; `gridSystem.ts` is Tier 1, so
  worth a designer answer before anyone changes either
- **Nothing validates that a `BP` key exists.** Deleting one emits
  `@media (min-width: undefined)`, which `recipeGuards.test.ts` does not check (it has no
  media-query validation), `tsc` accepts and lint ignores. This change was silent by that
  route too — a guard blind spot, noted rather than fixed
- **`footerShared.ts`'s `audit-allow` marker now sits 13 lines above its declaration.**
  Verified sound — lines 9–27 are one contiguous comment block — but a future edit that
  inserts a blank line there would silently un-acknowledge `'64em'`
- **`develop`'s registry is stale by more than this PR carries.** A full regeneration on
  `develop` produces an 18-line diff; the hook only staged what my commit's file set touched.
  Worth a housekeeping run.

3	description: "Marcel's review-verdict severity vs. author seniority: even a confirmed blocking-grade finding, or a scope/premise defect, can get waved through to full APPROVE when the PR author is senior/lateral"
4	metadata:

9	---
10	
11	When reviewing a colleague's PR (via zimmerMANNReview) and a finding is independently confirmed at must-fix/blocking severity, Marcel does not automatically choose a formal "Request Changes" verdict — he may deliberately choose comment-only, or even full approval, instead, even for a security-grade or scope-defining finding, when the author is senior or lateral (e.g. the project tech lead).
12	
13	**Example 1:** PR #75 (Tim Lavelle, tech lead) had a confirmed secret-leakage finding (`LHCI_SFDC_ACCESS_CONTROL` persisted in plaintext into a 30-day CI artifact + external LHCI server) — reproduced live, independently verified twice, no ambiguity in the technical claim. Given the choice between "Request changes" and "Comment only, let Tim triage," Marcel chose comment-only.
14	
15	**Example 2:** PR #79 (TimLavelleACC, same tech lead, SFCC-856 CSP hardening) had a finding I ranked #1 by cost-to-ignore — not just a code-quality issue but a scope/premise defect: the PR's own description claimed to close the Lighthouse `csp-xss` finding, but tracing `csp_evaluator`'s source confirmed `style-src` categorically cannot affect that audit's score (only `script-src`/`object-src`/`base-uri` can). I recommended "request changes" given that a false claim would close SFCC-856 on a wrong premise. Marcel overrode with "nothing but nitpicks, PR APPROVED" — folding even the premise-mismatch finding in with the genuine minor nitpicks (missing test, unshared constant) and approving outright, not just commenting.
16	
17	**Why:** the technical severity of a finding — and now, per example 2, even whether a finding is "just a nitpick" vs. "a scope/premise defect" — is judged on a separate axis from the *formal* review verdict. Seniority/lateral relationship is a legitimate input to the verdict axis itself, not just to comment phrasing. In both cases the underlying code was safe/correct to ship; the open item was documentation/framing (PR #79) or an already-otherwise-gated risk (PR #75, Tier-1 CODEOWNERS still pending). Marcel appears to weigh "is the code itself safe to merge" far more heavily than "is the PR's narrative 100% accurate" or "is this finding bigger than a nitpick" — a scope/premise issue fixable via a follow-up doc/ticket correction doesn't need to block the merge itself.
18	
19	**How to apply:** when presenting a PR review's adjudication questions, always ask the verdict question separately from "are the findings correct" — don't assume a confirmed must-fix finding, or a finding you'd personally rank above "nitpick," implies Request Changes. This is consistent with [[project_release_branch_status]]'s PR #75 entry and with zimmerMANNReview's own existing guidance to phrase blockers as questions (not directives) toward senior/lateral owners — this extends that same deference to the formal verdict mechanism itself (COMMENT/APPROVE vs REQUEST_CHANGES), not just comment wording. Calibrate your own recommendation accordingly: still surface a premise/scope defect clearly and rank it honestly, but don't over-weight it toward "should block" when the underlying code is sound and the author is senior/lateral — state it, recommend proportionately, and let Marcel make the actual call. Still ask each time rather than assuming approval is the default — the deciding factor was the author's seniority/relationship, not the finding's severity, so a similar finding against a junior contributor's PR or a lower-trust context might reasonably get the opposite call.

**State at pause (2026-08-28).** Branch `fix/footer-tablet-wide-breakpoint`, one commit pushed
(`21fca2f`), PR #69 OPEN and **APPROVED** but explicitly not to be merged. Three files modified
**stashed** (2026-08-28) as `stash@{0}`, message beginning *"PR #69 footer: 946px stack…"*:
`footer/footer.css.ts`, `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, `footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts`
— 3 files, +62/−21. Recover with `git stash pop stash@{0}`; verify by grepping the stash for
`sitemapInline`, `SIZE_COL_MAP_TABLET` and `flexWrap: 'wrap'`. **Stash numbering shifted** — the
older SFCC-89 PDP WIP is now `stash@{1}`, so index by message, not number. All gates were green (tsc 0, 379 Vitest, 98 Storybook,
lint/audit at develop's baseline, CodeRabbit no findings).

**Pushing will dismiss the approval** — `develop` has `dismissesStaleReviews: true`.

**Three questions block the commit, all for Kiera:**

1. **Bottom bar tablet padding.** Figma Legel (40000407:23786) is `px-[32px]`; we render 40px.
   The 40 is **Tim's** deliberate call (`5ecd515`, 23 Aug) with a written rationale that treats
   the 8px offset as a bug — Figma says it's intent (Content and Logo 40, Legel 32, tablet only;
   desktop is 40 everywhere). Not reverted, because overriding the lead's documented decision on
   a design read is a stop-and-ask under AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule.
2. **`SIZE_SUBSCRIBE_SLOT`.** Already flagged provisional at 45px; Figma's success state implies
   59px. Neither covers the **67px** the validation-error state actually needs.
3. **Does the field's error message sit inside the Textfield's box or below it?** We append
   below, which is what grows the slot. If the design keeps it inside a 320×44 box, no
   reservation change is needed at all. The four error-state nodes Marcel found
   (`QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` 8107:723/724/725/729) are **all deleted** — that file now has one
   page named `-----`, so there is nothing to reference.

**Measured, so it doesn't need re-deriving:** the validation error grows the control slot
45→67px (+22) at every breakpoint. Stacked (<946) everything below shifts down; inline (946+)
the site map holds and only logo/bar move. `SubscribePlaceholder`'s shift guard passes because
it exercises the *submit-unavailable* path (36px, fits) — the validation path was never covered.
Root cause is that the 45px reservation was derived from the idle state alone, so bumping the
number without a test across **all** states repeats the defect.

**Why:** three separate threads are parked mid-flight on one branch, and the approval on #69 is
stale relative to what's now in the working tree.

**How to apply:** don't commit or push until Kiera answers; when she does, batch all three.
See [[project-styling-layer-boundary]] and [[project-figma-metrics-rule]] — the two-Figma-file
trap applies here, the deleted nodes were from the composed-page file, not the design system.

I worked this as a single reviewer across the angles below (no Task/sub-agent tool was available in this environment — only `Read`/`Bash` — so I ran each angle as a dedicated, sequential deep-dive against the two worktrees and the base commit, rather than literally spawning parallel agents).
